env-api-keys-structure.title: prime-agent repo: credential resolution layout in packages/ai/src/env-api-keys.ts
env-api-keys-structure.content:
Repo /home/bench/work/repo (prime-agent v0.7.0), file packages/ai/src/env-api-keys.ts.

Credential lookup has two distinct layers:
1. Special-case `if` blocks ABOVE the `envMap` object; these override the map and are the only source of multi-var precedence lists:
   - anthropic -> ["ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN", "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"]
   - github-copilot -> ["COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN", "GH_TOKEN", "GITHUB_TOKEN"] (only 3-element list in the file)
2. `const envMap` — provider id -> single env var string. 28 entries. Keys are quoted only when they contain hyphens; values are read literally and do NOT derive mechanically from provider ids (e.g. vercel-ai-gateway -> AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, huggingface -> HF_TOKEN, google -> GEMINI_API_KEY). Vars are many-to-one across providers: moonshotai/moonshotai-cn share MOONSHOT_API_KEY, opencode/opencode-go share OPENCODE_API_KEY, cloudflare-workers-ai/cloudflare-ai-gateway share CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY. minimax-cn does NOT share with minimax (MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY).

Ambient (non-API-key) credential sources are read only inside `getEnvApiKey`, never in `getApiKeyEnvVars`/`envMap`. The file's own doc comment states these are intentionally excluded from env-key reporting:
- amazon-bedrock: AWS_PROFILE, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID + AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI, AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI, AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE
- google-vertex: ADC via GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, plus config-only GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT / GCLOUD_PROJECT / GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION. Its only mapped credential is GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY.

PRIME_TEAM_ID appears in the same file but is config, not a credential.

precedence semantics: `findEnvKeys`/`getEnvApiKey` use `envKeys?.[0]` first, so array order == precedence order.

matrix-json-task-result.title: Completed: provider -> credential env var matrix at /home/bench/results/matrix.json
matrix-json-task-result.content:
Task: map every member of the KnownProvider union (packages/ai/src/types.ts) to its credential env vars per packages/ai/src/env-api-keys.ts, omitting providers with no mapping. Output written as a bare JSON object (no fence, no prose) to /home/bench/results/matrix.json.

Status: DONE.

KnownProvider has 32 members. 30 are present in the output; 2 omitted:
- openai-codex: absent from envMap and from every special case; getApiKeyEnvVars returns undefined (OAuth-only provider).
- amazon-bedrock: no API-key mapping at all; getEnvApiKey only consults ambient AWS credentials, which the file documents as intentionally excluded from env-key reporting.

If this decision is challenged, the alternative reading would add amazon-bedrock with [AWS_PROFILE, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI, AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI, AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE]; the chosen reading follows the 'no credential env var mapping -> omit' instruction plus the file's own exclusion comment.

Multi-element entries in the output: anthropic (2), github-copilot (3). All others are single-element.

Extraction method that worked: read both files fully with open().read(), slice types.ts between 'export type KnownProvider' and 'export type Provider =' and regex `\t\| "([^"]+)"` for the union members; slice env-api-keys.ts between 'const envMap' and 'const envVar = envMap' and regex `"?([a-z0-9\-]+)"?:\s*"([A-Z0-9_]+)"` for the map. Special cases must be added by hand since they live outside envMap.
